chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man performing tamattuʿ who enters into iḥrām for hajj, then performs tawaf and saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah before his departure to Minā. He said: There is no harm in it.

So it does not conflict with the first report, because it is to be understood as applying to the elderly man, the fearful person, and the woman who fears menstruation. But when that excuse is absent, there is consensus that it is not permissible in any circumstance; this indicates that.

key_terms.الْحَيْضَ: menstruation, as a legal excuse affecting ritual performance
key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the earlier hadith report being reconciled with this one
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the sacred location to which pilgrims proceed during hajj rites
key_terms.يَسْعَى: performs saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.يُهِلُّ: enters into the ritual state and pronounces the talbiyah for hajj

ai.seo_question: Can a person performing tamattuʿ do the tawaf and saʿy of hajj before going to Minā?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on a person performing Hajj al-tamattuʿ who advances the tawaf and saʿy of hajj before departing to Minā. The report states permissibility, while the concluding juristic note clarifies that this is restricted to cases of excuse such as old age, fear, or a woman fearing menstruation; otherwise, it is not permitted.
